summary.text: The biological pump is the ocean's biologically driven movement of carbon from the air and land runoff into the deep ocean and seafloor sediments.
Phytoplankton fix carbon in the sunlit surface, and when organisms die their particles sink, often clumping into aggregates that fall much faster.
It moves about 10.2 gigatonnes of carbon into the ocean interior each year, and without it atmospheric carbon dioxide would be about 400 ppm higher.

facts.label: Reaching the seabed
facts.value: About 1% of particles leaving the surface

facts.label: Time in sediment
facts.value: May be stored for millions of years

items.prompt: Imagine the ocean's living things stopped carrying carbon down into the deep. What would happen to carbon dioxide in the air?

options.label: It would fall sharply
It would stay about the same
It would be much higher
It would only change by season

items.explain: An ocean without a biological pump would leave atmospheric carbon dioxide about 400 ppm higher than today.

items.prompt: Dead plankton and droppings often stick together into clumps as they sink. Why does that help their carbon reach the seafloor?

options.label: Clumps float until currents carry them to shore
Clumps sink faster, escaping being eaten or decomposed
Clumps are too hard for any bacteria to digest
Clumps trap air that pulls them downward

items.explain: Aggregation greatly speeds sinking, giving particles a better chance of escaping predation and decomposition on the way down.

items.prompt: Of all the particles that sink out of the surface ocean, roughly what share reaches the seabed?

options.label: About 1%
About 25%
About half
Nearly all of them

items.explain: Only about 1% of particles leaving the surface reach the seabed; most are consumed or respired on the way.

items.prompt: A coccolithophore builds itself a protective calcium carbonate coating. Which part of the pump does that coating feed?

options.label: The soft-tissue pump
The physical pump
The nitrogen pump
The carbonate pump

items.explain: Calcium carbonate formed into shells and coatings is cycled by the carbonate pump; organic matter goes through the soft-tissue pump.

items.prompt: Upwelling regions fix 2 to 3 times more carbon per area than the open ocean. Why does the open ocean still fix most of the ocean's carbon?

options.label: It covers far more of the ocean's area
Its plankton work faster in deep water
Upwelling regions only work in winter
Its water holds more dissolved oxygen

items.explain: The open ocean makes up more than 90% of the ocean's area, so it fixes about 80% of the carbon despite lower output per area.

items.prompt: Carbon carried into the deep ocean as dissolved inorganic carbon does not stay there forever. How does it get back to the air?

options.label: Storms churn it up within a few weeks
Deep ocean circulation returns it over millennia
Fish carry it up on their nightly swims
Undersea volcanoes blast it to the surface

items.explain: Thermohaline circulation brings deep-ocean dissolved inorganic carbon back to the atmosphere on timescales of thousands of years.
